rules: Characters must feel alive: use lib.js setFace() every frame (brows, eye size, mouth shape, pupil look direction) with a different expression for each beat, then life() for breathing, blinking, glances and idle sway. Characters react to every event (shock, cringe, look at the damage).

Add at least one other character who reacts: a neighbor, a pet, a family member. Use 3–6 short speech bubbles (drawBubble, 1–3 words, funny) anchored to heads, as in the reference videos ('Still good.', 'MY HAT!').

Big events are EXPANDING WAVES, never a beam or a single flash: makeShockwave() (dust wall ring, glowing shell, ground ring) plus a reaction in the world as the front passes (suburb.wave(): roofs rip off and tumble, trees flatten, cars slide). Each topic gets its own fitting spreading effect (a heat wave that browns lawns outward, a frost front, a crack network, a flood front, etc.).
Aerial/city shots use makeSuburb(): a block grid with streets both ways, gable roofs, lawns, driveways, trees, cars and pools. No plain boxes on a flat green plane.

Numbers sit on the left side as a small counter (drawSideCounter: small label, big number, italic comparison note like 'faster than sound'), placed under the title, as in the reference videos. Never a big box in the middle of the screen. Keep the right edge clear (platform buttons).

Sound: always a background song (music2.song: drums, bass, arp, lead that build with the intensity curve) plus environment beds (music2.amb: city/wind/space/fire) under the voice and SFX. Music must sit clearly under the voice (music_gain ≈ 0.38, amb gain ≈ 0.25–0.3).
Also export a no-music version for TikTok (music_gain 0), so the owner can add a trending sound in the app (copyrighted songs are never baked into the file).
Busy, living world (owner, Nov 9): pedestrians walking on the sidewalks, cars actually driving on the streets (not only parked), more bystanders who all react (stop, point, run, film with phones).
Anything flying through the sky shares it with planes/helicopters/birds that pass close by (the flying person passes a plane, a passenger at the window reacts).

Breakage must read instantly: when something punches through a wall/door, the hole is a crisp cartoon cut-out of its exact silhouette (star pose, arms and legs out), shown in a 0.5 s slow-motion beat from the far side with light shining through the hole and dust puffing out of the outline, then debris bursts outward. Never a random scatter of blocks.
Pacing (owner, Nov 9 — middle point between our 4 s and the reference's 1.4 s): a new shot or a big camera move every ~2–2.5 s.
Use a continuous follow-camera when it helps (e.g. follow the character while he flies instead of cutting away).

2–4 object close-ups/inserts per video (the cat mid-air, the hat, the mailbox, a glass shard, a bystander's phone screen filming it). Keep inventing small interactive touches like these — the owner wants more of them.
The counter changes meaning per chapter (e.g. SNEEZE SPEED → DISTANCE FLOWN → TIME TO LANDING) and always moves: ticking decimals, colour shifts to orange/red as danger rises.

Every milestone gets a real-world comparison SHOWN on screen, side by side, with a small label (a jet next to the sneeze wind, a bullet racing it, a rocket at escape velocity, a satellite) so viewers instantly get what the number means.
Name tags only for a character's first appearance (intro), optional.
Recurring cast links the episodes (shared universe): MITTENS the cat appears regularly (give her a proper intro the first time — people love animals), plus Dave the neighbour and the main character.
Special cartoon faces at peak moments: heart eyes, star eyes, tears, sweat drop, dizzy swirl.
Occasionally (not every video) a fake live-chat/phone-comment overlay or a background bystander shouting a funny line.
Floating particles (embers, dust motes, sparkles) present but subtle — not too much, not too little.
Ending: return to the opening scene but changed (loop + twist), then the question, then a 'Part 2' tease.

Title (owner loved the 'boyfriend' reference, Nov 9): flash cold open (0.5 s of the craziest moment + one punch word like 'SNIP.'), then the title types in word by word over a wide establishing shot, holds ~3 s and then animates OUT (by ~5 s). After that only the side counter stays at the top. Optional time-jump card ('⏮ 3 minutes earlier').
Counter sub-label shows place + time and updates with the story ('YOUR APARTMENT · 9:41 PM' → 'DOWNTOWN · 9:43 PM' → 'EARTH ORBIT').

Talking characters: short punchy speech bubbles in quick back-and-forth (white rounded bubble, 2–6 words), mouths moving while they talk, extreme close-up faces for big reactions (huge eyes, wide open mouth), countdown numbers (3, 2, 1) popping next to the bubbles when tension builds.
Crowds: when the story scales up, show LOTS of people (hundreds to thousands, instanced) filling streets, plus people in the background of normal shots.
Buildings with detail: lit windows, varied facades and heights, dusk/evening light when it fits — never plain boxes.

Switch perspective when it matters: first-person (hands on the steering wheel, hands holding the object) for the start or key moments, then third-person behind/side views, and back to first-person for the ending (owner approved Nov 9). Body/'what if YOU' premises: short POV start; calm world/history premises can stay mostly POV; comedy/action stays mostly third-person.
Shareable ending line when it fits the topic (e.g. 'Send this to your boyfriend.') instead of only 'follow'.

rules: PREMISE: happens to the WHOLE WORLD (not one person), with a short time limit: 'What if <something basic> <vanished/doubled/stopped> for 5 seconds?'. History premises ('what if the asteroid missed') are also fine.

Then 'it comes back' and the aftermath.

rules: *** STANDARD.md in the repo root is now the owner's OFFICIAL list (Nov 17) and overrides every rule in this list where they differ. Read it first. ***

*** RUNAWAY FORMAT (owner approved Nov 16 - THIS OVERRIDES the 'STRUCTURE', 'ONE big visual transformation' and 'OPENING STAKE' rules below wherever they conflict; applies to every video built from Nov 18 on) *** PREMISE: a process that never stops and keeps multiplying ('every fold doubles the paper', 'the hole just keeps going', 'Mittens never stops growing') - NOT 'X for 5 seconds', no slow motion, no countdown. STRUCTURE (50-65 s): 0-3 s title on screen + hero in today's everyday place, counter already visible at its small starting value; the process starts by second 3. Then 10-13 STEPS of 4-5 s each: at every step (a) the COUNTER jumps (animated roll-up, drawSideCounter) and its unit escalates wildly (mm -> m -> km -> 'past the Moon'; kg -> tonnes -> 'heavier than the Titanic'), (b) ONE short italic line with a REAL, checked comparison, read by the narrator, (c) the picture visibly changes, (d) the camera keeps pulling back in one continuous move: room -> street -> city -> country -> planet -> space. Early (human-scale) steps carry the comedy: cast reactions, narrator blaming the hero. Mittens cam reacts at every step. Last step = the biggest image + punchline, then the end card. Every number must be computed in the script JSON (store the formula) - never invented. Never copy another channel's exact premise or shots.

*** CLEAR WRITING (owner, Nov 17, about the jump video: 'confusing... it wasn't really clear... the things said and how jokes were made are strange'; everything else - quality, characters, city - he liked) *** (1) LISTEN TEST: the narration ALONE must tell a complete, simple story a 12-year-old follows on the first listen - what is happening, what happens next, and why. Never rely on the picture to explain a line. (2) ONE THREAD: line 1 sets up the hero's small everyday stake (the unpaid bill, the ice cream) and the story keeps returning to it; the last line pays it off. (3) EVERY JOKE NEEDS A SETUP the viewer already saw or heard. Banned unless set up earlier in the same video: 'This was your idea, by the way', 'You had one job', a random bystander line ('He picked this moment to propose'), facts that need a second to decode ('Pigeons are dinosaurs', 'Mittens is not a person'). (4) At most ONE joke per step, and it should come from the consequence on screen (what the counter or the world just did), not a random aside. (5) Short concrete sentences (12 words max), plain words, one idea per line. No abstract or time-travel framing ('history gets one tiny edit', 'it arrives seven minutes late'). (6) The closing 'strangest part' fact must be instantly understandable: one simple comparison (not 'less than a thousandth of the width of an atom'). (7) Before rendering, write all lines in a list and check each one against 1-6; rewrite any that fail. GOOD model: engine/scripts/paperfold.json (one thread - the bill - numbers that climb, jokes tied to each step, payoff 'you still have to pay it'). BAD model: engine/scripts/jump.json and asteroid.json (disconnected one-liners, unset-up callbacks).

STRUCTURE (45–55 s): (1) 0–7 s calm, lived-in everyday scene, title on screen (types in, leaves by ~6 s) and a real-time countdown '<EVENT> IN 0:07.000' on the left; (2) the event; the story's 5 seconds play in ~6x SLOW MOTION over ~30 s while the counter shows '<THING> RETURNS IN 0:04.779' ticking in milliseconds; (3) it returns, ~6 s real-time aftermath, counter relabelled ('SUNLIGHT: BACK'); (4) 6 s end card.

NO cold open, no 'N seconds earlier' card, no speech bubbles, no punch captions, no word-by-word ASS captions. Text on screen = title, countdown, and one short italic serif line every 3–4 s addressed to 'you' (the narrator reads exactly those lines).

NARRATOR: yes (Kokoro af_heart, speed 1.0), reading the italic lines. 1–2 videos this month go out with NO narrator (music + lines only, cue like sun_cue_novoice.json) as a test: mark them `no_narrator_test: true` in the queue. Suggested: Nov 16 and Nov 24. UPDATE Nov 15 (owner): the Nov 16 video DOES get the narrator (the comedy needs it); only Nov 24 remains as the no-narrator test.
CAMERA: one continuous moving camera with at most 2–3 cuts (street → look up → rise over the city → back to a face).

ONE big visual transformation that a 10-year-old understands instantly and that keeps growing (sky goes black and the city lights up; everything floats; water vanishes). Not a list of small unrelated effects. Check the science and keep the lines accurate.

A LIVELY STREET (owner): more cars driving and more people doing specific things in the calm opening and aftermath — someone walking a dog, a jogger, a cyclist, someone on the phone, kids with balloons, a street musician, a delivery van unloading, pedestrians passing close to the camera. Never an empty street.

END CARD + COMMENTS (owner approved): black card with the title, one small line of facts, then 'What should we try next?' / 'TELL US IN THE COMMENTS'. Add to every caption: 'Comment your what-if — we make the best ones.' When a queue item has `idea_from` (a viewer's public handle), show 'Idea from a viewer comment' for the first 3 s and credit the @handle in the caption. NEVER offer prizes, giveaways or 'like/subscribe to be picked' (YouTube spam policy), never ask for likes or subs in the video.
SOUND: narrator always clearly on top (mix.py enforces a 14 dB margin; music_gain ≤ 0.3, sfx_gain ≤ 0.4). Quiet, tense bed during the slow motion; ticks; a riser into the return.

KEEP: New-York-style detailed city (or another equally detailed real-feeling place when the idea needs it), Mittens as a small background detail, AI labels on TikTok/Instagram and 'Animated · AI voice' in the YouTube description, a no-music copy for the owner's TikTok post.

OPENING STAKE (owner, Nov 11): the first 5 seconds must not be a still scene plus a question. Give 'you' (or one visible person) a small, specific thing in progress that the event interrupts — about to take a photo, a kid's balloon slipping away, a coffee being handed over, a proposal on one knee, a dog pulling its leash — and say it in the first italic line. Show how that small story ends in the aftermath (the photo, the balloon, the coffee), so the video pays off twice.
ANSWER LAST: keep the biggest, most surprising consequence for the final seconds before the end card; never give it away in the opening lines or the title.

POLISH STANDARD (owner, Nov 12: 'make them much more polished'): the engine now does this for every video - soft shadows, soft image-based fill light, colour grade and tilt-shift background blur in engine/page.html; rounded smooth characters (makePerson), rounded cars with wheels (carGeos) and rounded crowd (pedGeos) in engine/scenes/lib.js; framed windows with depth in the city shader. In new scene code: NEVER flatShading, never bare BoxGeometry for anything near the camera (use RoundedBoxGeometry exported from lib.js, Capsule/Sphere with >=16 segments), give the hero's surroundings real detail (window frames, sills, awnings, lamps, plants). Blur: return focusY (0..1 screen height of the subject, default 0.56) and focusH from update() so the hero is always in the sharp band; dof: 0 only for full-screen space shots.

DIFFERENT PLACE EVERY VIDEO (owner, Nov 12): each video opens small and human with the hero somewhere new, doing an everyday thing - walking down the street, slouching on the couch, at the dining table, in a restaurant, on a date, at the office, on a bus, in a park, at the gym, in bed. Never reuse the previous two videos' opening place. The place supplies the OPENING STAKE. Title, countdown, slow-motion structure, captions and end card stay identical so the channel is still recognisable. Record the place in the queue item as `place`.

MITTENS = THE FRIEND (owner, Nov 12): Mittens is the hero's companion in every video - always near the hero in the opening, gets one clear reaction shot or gag during the event (2 s max) and one in the aftermath. Never just a far background detail.

LANDMARK LABELS: when the camera passes something big or far (a tower, a bridge, the Moon, a plane), show one small label with its real name and a real number (height, distance, speed) for ~2 s. 2-4 labels per video, checked facts only.

BRIGHT LOOK (owner, Nov 15: 'still a bit dark'; reference = glossy toy-style reel): every shot must read bright and colourful on a phone. Recipe: strong warm key light on the hero (DirectionalLight ~3.0, colour 0xfff0d8) + cool blue rim/back light (~1.2, 0x7fb0ff) + hemisphere fill >= 0.9; saturated candy colours for clothes, cars, shop fronts and props; sunny daytime with blue sky by default; exposure 1.1-1.25. Night or dark topics: keep the world dark blue (never grey/black) and light the hero and props with warm lamps, neon and glowing objects so faces stay bright. Check 3 stills before the full render: if the hero's face is not the brightest, most colourful thing in frame, fix the lights first.

VARIED CITY (owner, Nov 15: 'the city is bland, all the same'): no two neighbouring buildings alike - vary colour (brick red, cream, teal, mustard, pink, pale blue), height, roof type and ground floor (cafe with awning, bakery, bookshop, pharmacy with neon cross, laundromat, flower stand); add trees, benches, street lamps, signs with short invented names, parked bikes, a mural, bunting. At least 6 distinct shop fronts on the hero's street.

TONE = COMEDY (owner, Nov 15): narrator keeps exactly the same calm voice (af_heart) - NOT angry, NO swearing - but the lines are dry jokes instead of explanations. APPROVED GAGS: (1) NARRATOR AGAINST THE HERO (owner: 'I love this'): the narrator calmly blames the hero for everything ('You had one job. It was holding the keys.'), 2-3 such lines per video. (2) MITTENS STEALS THE SCENE: whatever disaster happens the cat is fine and mildly annoyed/unimpressed - use setCatFace(cat, mood) + catLife(cat, t) from lib.js (moods: neutral, unimpressed, annoyed, shock, happy, sleepy, smug, scared); give Mittens at least 3 mood changes and 2 close shots where the face is readable. (3) THE ONE UNBOTHERED PERSON: everyone panics while one bystander calmly carries on (eating a sandwich, reading the paper, watering plants, doing yoga, on a phone call) - a different activity each video. At least one visual joke every ~6 s. Aftermath ends on a punchline with the science fact folded in. Still accurate - never invent facts. NOT approved yet (owner decides later): meme-style edits (freeze-frames, zooms, record scratch) and random absurd cameos (the skeleton).

FLUENT MOTION (owner, Nov 15): no stiff or sliding characters - walk cycles with arm swing, bounce and head bob; every reaction has anticipation and follow-through (easeInOut, small overshoot); hero is never frozen (use life()). During the slow-motion section something new must happen at least every 4 s (average viewer leaves at ~22 s): a new object affected, a new gag, a camera move - never one idea held for 10 s.

BACKGROUND CAST (owner, Nov 15): a recurring cast of side characters; each video uses 2-3 of them (never all), different combination from the previous video, each with a fixed look so viewers recognise them. Record who appeared in the queue item as `cast`. FAVOURITES: THE FILMER (records everything on a phone instead of helping, complains about the lighting); THE SALESMAN (already selling T-shirts/souvenirs about the disaster seconds in); THE PIGEON (one pigeon watches and judges); BAD TIMING (someone proposing / carrying a wedding cake / taking a driving test at the exact wrong second); THE UNBOTHERED PERSON (keeps eating a sandwich etc.). USE RARELY: THE COMPLAINER ('my coffee's cold' after the world resets); THE OVER-REACTOR (screams before anything happens - owner finds it a bit cringe, max once every 5 videos, keep it short). Mittens is in every video and does not count toward the 2-3.

GOLDEN LIGHT (owner, Nov 15, three reference videos: 'I like the lighting in all of them, we should copy it'): default outdoor light = warm low sun (late afternoon): DirectionalLight colour ~0xffd9a8, intensity ~3, low angle (25-35 degrees) so shadows are long and soft; sky gradient pale blue to warm cream at the horizon; warm-tinted atmospheric haze (scene.fog, FogExp2 or equivalent) so distant buildings fade softly; some windows lit warm; cool blue fill in the shadows. Interiors: a visible warm lamp, pastel walls, wooden floor, coloured props. Space shots: bright saturated Earth with a thin blue atmosphere rim. This replaces flat midday light.

BUILDING STYLE (owner, Nov 15, reference = European street in the 'getting fat' video): street-level buildings are 4-6 storey town houses in warm colours (ochre, cream, terracotta, pale pink), each with window shutters, balconies with railings, cornices, pitched or mansard roofs with chimneys, a ground-floor shop with a painted sign (invented names), awnings, cobbled or paved street. Tall glass towers only in the distance. Build these as real geometry near the camera (not a flat shader wall).

MITTENS CAM (owner, Nov 16: 'Mittens still has little to no emotions'): every video shows a round picture-in-picture close-up of Mittens' face (lib.js makeCatCam; return `inset: { scene: mc.scene, camera: mc.camera, x: 0.8, y: 0.2, r: 0.15, show }` from update()). Call mc.update(t, mood) every frame and CHANGE THE MOOD AT EVERY STEP (unimpressed, annoyed, shock, smug, sleepy, happy, scared) so her reaction is the running joke; pop it in at the first step, hide it (show -> 0) during the title and end card. Mittens must ALSO appear in the scene itself near the hero in the opening.

HAIR (owner, Nov 16: the hair blobs/tufts 'don't look natural at all' - removed): makePerson hair is now ONE smooth shell hugging the head, nothing on top. hairStyle: 'short' (default) | 'long' (adds a flat back panel) | 'bald'. Vary hair COLOUR across the cast, not shape. NEVER add tufts, fringes, buns, blobs, headbands or caps on top of a head unless it is a deliberate prop (helmet, chef hat). The owner may send a reference hairstyle to replicate - until then keep it this simple. Hero: hairStyle 'short', hair 0x5a3a20.

IMAGE QUALITY (owner, Nov 16: 'the video itself could be of better quality'): the engine now renders with 4x anti-aliasing (page.html, default) and a lighter background blur. Final encode: upscale with `-vf scale=1080:1920:flags=lanczos,unsharp=5:5:0.55:5:5:0.0` and `-crf 20 -maxrate 9M -bufsize 18M`. Never let a blurred foreground object (car, lamp post) cover more than ~10% of the frame. Keep the subject large: the hero or the main object should fill at least a third of the frame height in close and medium shots.

YOUTUBE UPLOAD (from a Shorts tutorial the owner sent, Nov 16 - cheap to apply, unproven): title = premise with the first two words in capitals ('WHAT IF every fold doubled the paper? 📄'), one emoji, under 60 characters, leave curiosity open; hashtags: maximum 5 in total, always #shorts plus 3-4 specific to the topic (no generic piles); description: 1-2 punchy sentences, then one line of comma-separated topic keywords, then the same hashtags.
